article_title: Reading Apprenticeship
citation: Reading Apprenticeship. (2024). Evidence for ESSA program review. https://www.evidenceforessa.org
title: Integrating metacognitive strategy instruction into content-area courses with collaborative sense-making
description: All Reading Apprenticeship variations share a common instructional design: they integrate metacognitive strategy instruction into subject-area teaching rather than a stand-alone reading curriculum. As the review states, the programs "incorporate extensive reading, collaborative sense-making, and teaching of meta-cognitive skills such as prediction, summarization, graphic organizers, and clarification." Teachers model reasoning processes so strategies are learned in the context of authentic content reading.
requirements: Teachers receive extensive professional development and coaching, including analyses of classroom video and modeling of reasoning processes
target_learners: high school students in science and social studies, including struggling readers
target_learning_goals: metacognitive reading strategies such as prediction, summarization, graphic organizers, and clarification
examples: RAAL classrooms use document cameras, Post-its for students' annotations, and video viewing to support the strategies

Reading achievement

article_title: Organizing Early Education for Improvement
citation: Ehrlich, S.B., Pacchiano, D.M., Stein, A.G., Wagner, M.R., Luppescu, S., Park, S., Frank, E., Lewandowski, H., & Young, C. (2018). Organizing early education for improvement: Testing a new survey tool. Chicago, IL: University of Chicago Consortium on School Research and the Ounce of Prevention Fund. https://consortium.uchicago.edu/
title: Use explicit Rasch-based criteria (reliability, item fit, difficulty spread, DIF) when developing survey measures
description: The report used the Rasch IRT model rather than raw-score methods because IRT "creates measures that are on linear scales," provides a person standard error, and handles missing data without bias. Measure refinement followed explicit criteria: person reliability of at least 0.70 (preferably above 0.80), item fit with infit mean square below 1.30, adequate spread of item difficulty, and removal of items with significant and large DIF contrasts. Rasch also "allows for comparisons over time" by equating measures across respondent samples.
requirements: Items must fit the restricted one-parameter Rasch model; some items may need to be discarded or modified to fit
Measures should reach person reliability of at least 0.70, with reliabilities greater than 0.80 preferred
constraints: A disadvantage of Rasch analysis is that some items may need to be discarded or modified to fit the model
target_learners: survey developers and researchers measuring organizational or educational constructs
ECE program staff who receive survey reports
target_learning_goals: producing reliable, unidimensional survey measures that validly capture respondents' perceptions and can be tracked over time
examples: Items with significant (p < 0.05) and large (p > 0.50) DIF contrasts were considered for removal, though some large-DIF items were retained when they fit within each group

article_title: Evaluating AI Tutoring at the Speed of Innovation: Practitioner-Led Micro-Randomised Trials of an AI Tutoring Platform in GCSE Science
citation: Wayne Harrison, Rahil Khowaja, Emma Dobson, Germaine Uwimpuhwe, and Steve Higgins. (2026). Evaluating AI Tutoring at the Speed of Innovation: Practitioner-Led Micro-Randomised Trials of an AI Tutoring Platform in GCSE Science. https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14789v1
title: Rapid cumulative micro-RCT evaluation architecture: signal, replication, accumulation
description: An evaluation architecture for rapidly evolving educational AI in which practitioner-led micro-randomised controlled trials are repeated across cohorts, contexts and product versions. Its value lies "not in replacing definitive evaluation with small studies, but in enabling a rapid, cumulative evaluation architecture in which randomised estimates can be generated, replicated and updated". Three linked stages structure the model: an initial trial generates a provisional causal signal; replication tests whether direction and magnitude recur; accumulation characterises the distribution of effects across versions, pedagogy, populations and implementation. Successive estimates are represented through forest plots and cumulative meta-analysis, retaining individual estimates rather than allowing a pooled mean to obscure heterogeneity.
requirements: Random allocation embedded in routine practice, with secure randomisation separating allocation and analysis from teacher judgement
Common protocols, transparent reporting, consistent core outcomes and explicit version documentation across cycles
constraints: Individual micro-RCTs provide only provisional estimates; engagement analytics are post-randomisation and cannot support causal inference
The randomised intention-to-treat contrast should remain the causal centre of the evidence
target_learners: Secondary school students (Year 9 and Year 10) in mainstream English schools
target_learning_goals: GCSE science attainment in extended written answers to curriculum-aligned examination questions
examples: The Medly evaluation embedded three parallel subject-specific micro-RCTs in routine revision practice over four weeks, using the WhatWorked Teachers platform for randomisation and automated ANCOVA reporting.

article_title: Agentic AI-driven Immersive Simulation: A Knowledge-Aware Virtual Training Platform for High Dose Rate (HDR) Brachytherapy
citation: Ronghua Xu, Kepha Barasa, Manoj Kumal, Xinyun Liu, Weihua Zhou, Xin Qian. (2026). Agentic AI-driven Immersive Simulation: A Knowledge-Aware Virtual Training Platform for High Dose Rate (HDR) Brachytherapy. arXiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08163
title: RAG-based cognitive backend grounding assistant responses in HDR brachytherapy guidelines
description: The backend functions as an intelligent tutor built on a RAG pipeline: guideline documents are parsed, split into 512-token chunks with overlap, embedded (nomic-embed-text or MedEmbed), and indexed in a FAISS vector store. At query time a hybrid dense-plus-sparse retrieval performs cosine-similarity search, and retrieved chunks are synthesized by an LLM (e.g., GPT-4o-mini) into actionable instructions delivered via TTS. The article states this grounds responses "strictly grounded in the medical literature," mitigating hallucination risk.
requirements: Authoritative HDR brachytherapy guideline documents for ingestion; an embedding model, FAISS index, STT module (OpenAI Whisper), LLM, and TTS module
constraints: Its ability to provide answers is limited by the quality and number of documents it can reference; the standardized guideline set cannot account for institution-specific protocols, practitioner preferences, or unusual scenarios
target_learners: medical trainees practicing brachytherapy procedures
target_learning_goals: receiving real-time, evidence-based procedural guidance during training
examples: The four-stage RAG pipeline (preprocess, knowledge retrieval, actionable generation, post-process) is implemented with Langchain, PyPDF, FAISS, Ollama, Flask, Whisper, FastAPI, and ngrok in the prototype

citation: Hung-Yue Suen and Kuo-En Hung. (2026). An Interpretable Closed-Loop Intelligent Tutoring System for Multimodal Affective Feedback in Asynchronous Presentation Training. IEEE Transactions on Learning Technologies. https://doi.org/10.1109/TLT.2026.3693864
title: Retrieval-augmented Conversational AI Tutor with modular GROW-aligned coaching routines
description: The Conversational AI Tutor is a retrieval-grounded conversational module built on GPT-4.1 with a RAG layer that anchors each response in the learner's own multimodal records (transcripts, BARS scores, emotion descriptors, feature summaries) and maintains records across submissions for longitudinal reflection. The tutor implements three modular routines—performance summarization, strength and weakness highlighting, and translation of analytic indicators into learner-facing concepts—with phrasing drawn from a curated library of expert coaching aligned to the BARS rubric and the GROW model (Goals, Reality, Options, Will).

citation: Shahin Hossain, Sima Ahmadi, Leqi Li, Idowu David Awoyemi, Wei Huang, Chenxi Zhou, Jujia Li, Samaa Haniya, Shapla Khanam, Tasbirun Mashreka Subaha. (2026). title: RAIL-Ed framework: responsible GenAI literacy for K–12 teachers as six interdependent pillars
description: RAIL-Ed is a justice-centered architecture for GenAI literacy in K–12 teacher education, spanning pre-service and in-service teachers. It defines GenAI literacy for teachers as "the integrated capacity of teachers to understand how generative systems produce outputs, to evaluate those outputs critically, to collaborate with them in pedagogically and ethically responsible ways, and to exercise principled agency, including restraint, over their role in learning." Six pillars operationalize this definition, grounded in Freirean critical pedagogy, Deweyan inquiry, Vygotskian sociocultural theory, and Shneiderman's human-centered AI. Equity is built in as a constitutive commitment rather than a separate pillar.
requirements: Each pillar must name a capacity whose absence produces a distinct, documented pedagogical failure; each must admit a distinct developmental trajectory; and each must be groundable in the four theoretical traditions
constraints: The framework is conceptual and awaiting empirical validation; the authors state it does not provide empirical validation or present a finalized product

K–12 in-service teachers
target_learning_goals: GenAI literacy: understanding generative systems, critical evaluation of outputs, responsible human–AI collaboration, ethical reasoning, and principled agency

article_title: From RAMSing to Rigor: Improving Moderator Analysis in STEM Education Meta-Research
citation: Bicakci, M., Heller, F., Stoeger, H., & Ziegler, A. (2026). From RAMSing to Rigor: Improving Moderator Analysis in STEM Education Meta-Research. Educational Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-026-10172-1
title: RAMSing: reporting after moderators are significant
description: RAMSing is the article's name for a selective reporting practice in meta-research: "the practice of conducting multiple moderator tests but reporting only those effect sizes that meet conventional significance thresholds (e.g., p < .05) or exceed conventional effect-size benchmarks (e.g., d = 0.20, d = 0.50), while omitting the remaining results from the published record." It is distinguished from p-hacking, HARKing, and study-level publication bias because it operates within the meta-analysis itself. By suppressing null effect sizes it can inflate apparent explanatory power of moderator analyses, compress effect size distributions, and distort heterogeneity estimates, while obscuring true boundary conditions for theory and practice.
requirements: Detection requires explicit auditing of planned versus reported analyses where available, bias-robust statistical adjustment, and routine reporting of adequately powered moderator tests
constraints: The article notes only about half of moderator analyses are ever published, so observable red flags likely reveal only a subset of the problem
target_learners: STEM education meta-researchers
researchers in fields relying on meta-analytic moderator evidence
target_learning_goals: Understanding selective reporting bias in moderator analysis
Interpreting moderator evidence with appropriate caution
examples: Full-text screening of more than 100 STEM meta-analyses found indicators including moderators announced in introductions but absent from results, inconsistent summary tables, and vague statements such as "no other moderators were significant" without accompanying statistics

article_title: Some observations on the learning of sensible material.
citation: Dell, John A. (1911). Some Observations on the Learning of Sensible Material. Journal of Educational Psychology, 2, 401-406.
title: Rational learning builds associations by similarity with prior knowledge rather than by contiguity, explaining the absence of serial-position effects for sensible material
description: The article proposes a mechanism account contrasting nonsense-syllable learning with the learning of sensible material. With meaningless syllables, connections depend "almost entirely on their contiguity in space or time", which yields the serial-position curve Bolton showed. In rational learning, associations "depend almost entirely on associations by similarity with various facts", many outside the memorized series; the learner builds up concurrent mental series and places each new fact in its correct position in one of them. This account explains why position in the presented series had negligible influence on recall in all three experiments.
requirements: The material must be a series of facts having a rational relation to one another, so learners can connect new facts to pre-existing knowledge by similarity
constraints: The account is offered as the authors' interpretation of the three experiments, not as a separately tested prediction
target_learners: schoolboys in secondary forms
target_learning_goals: retention of meaningful lesson and lecture content

Where ratios "differ greatly from unity it is safe to draw deductions", but where the differences are small, nothing can be inferred, because a young group's extra score on one test must be compensated by slightly lower scores on other tests when totals are matched. The method therefore supports only an order of merit among tests, not absolute quantitative estimates.

citation: Omar David Perez & Gonzalo P. Urcelay. (2025). Delayed rewards weaken human goal directed actions. npj Science of Learning 10:36. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-025-00325-2
title: Perez and Dickinson's rate-correlation theory of goal-directed control
description: The article adopts the theory of Perez and Dickinson, in which a goal-directed system computes the correlation between response rate and outcome rate, holding responses and outcomes in contiguous working-memory slots. As the article states, "goal-directed strength is determined by subjects'experienced correlation between action and outcome rates and is directly related to instrumental performance and sensitivity to outcome revaluation." The theory explains why "Delays disrupt this experienced correlation, weakening goal- directed control", integrating the observed effects of delay on response rates, revaluation sensitivity and contingency knowledge, and it accounts for why ratio training supports higher rates than interval training.

constraints: When rewards are delayed, empty time samples assign the context a causal relationship with the outcome, weakening goal-directed control until the contextual association is extinguished.

target_learning_goals: Formation of action-outcome (instrumental contingency) knowledge and sensitivity to changes in outcome value
examples: The authors state the framework "integrates the observed effects of delay on revaluation sensitivity, response rates, and action-outcome contingency knowledge" in their stockbroker task.

title: Rapid formation of abstract parsing-event memories as a mechanism for within-seconds skill generalization
description: The article proposes that abstract structural memories, specifically shared parsing cue structures (two sequences composed of different keypresses that start and end with the same keypress), can form within seconds and generalize to new skills. citation: Salazar, D. A. (2015). Razalas' Grouping Method and Mathematics Achievement. Journal of Education and Practice, Vol.6, No.8. http://www.iiste.org
title: Razalas' Method of Grouping
description: An inverse grouping method used at the seatwork stage of Direct Instruction, reversing Salazar's Method: "the first stage is an individual competition and the next stages, a group member is added based on the student choice until the group has three members". Groups of three defend solutions for 5 bonus points each; the member who presented is eliminated to work individually, groups shrink to two then one, and membership must change each round. Accumulated points are ranked and added to the final examination score.

Bonus point incentives (5 points per successful defense) added to final examination scores
Group membership must not be the same in the next groupings

Female students in one section were excluded due to cultural orientation

target_learning_goals: Problem-solving in Integral Calculus (areas under curves, area between curves, volumes of solid revolution)
examples: In the experiment, the experimental group began with three-member groups of their choice; the member who discussed the group's solution was eliminated and worked individually in the next stage, cycling until the end of the trimester.

title: Buzan's radiant-thinking account of the mind map as a whole-brain graphic organizer
description: The article adopts Buzan's mind map theory, under which a mind map is "a type of graphic organizer" that makes visible what happens when the brain stores information. Its structure embodies "radiant thinking": the title sits at the center and sub-ideas diverge in all directions via curved links whose strength varies with distance from the center, using words, images and colors. The article links this to Ausubel's meaningful learning, in which learners link new information to prior knowledge, and uses it to explain why mind maps might aid comprehension.
requirements: learners link new learning activities with prior knowledge for meaningful learning to occur
constraints: the brain-hemisphere rationale is the article's interpretive account, not a tested result of this study
target_learners: school students learning English as a foreign language
target_learning_goals: organizing ideas, comprehension, and recall of text information
examples: The study's maps placed the main topic in a central shape with colored, tapering curved lines to sub-topics, topped by sub-ideas and supplemented with images and symbols

Placement test to decide the step at which children begin the intervention

beginner readers in early primary school

reading fluency
grapheme-phoneme correspondences and phoneme blending

recognizing structural inequality and racial stereotypes

title: Rasch Learning Gain: a psychometric benchmark for estimating learning gain
description: Rasch Learning Gain is defined as the difference between estimated posttest and pretest latent abilities (RLG=(θpost−θpre)) on the Rasch measurement scale, serving as an estimate of individual learning gain across an instructional intervention. The article applied the dichotomous 1-parameter logistic Rasch model with conditional maximum likelihood estimation for item parameters and maximum likelihood estimation for person abilities. Because the Rasch model allows estimation of individual students' abilities independently of the specific test items used, it is widely applied in educational measurement and medical education research, and served as the benchmark method in this study.
requirements: Requires substantially larger samples to ensure stable estimation of item parameters and person abilities
constraints: Rasch model-based estimation requires larger sample sizes to obtain stable parameter estimates, making it inapplicable to very small datasets

description: Rational emotive behavior education is described as "An outgrowth of rational emotive behavior therapy", which Albert Ellis first used in the mid-1950s to alter erroneous beliefs so they can be replaced by rational ones. constraints: The article notes REBE theorists' concepts (self-esteem versus self-acceptance) need to be spread throughout institutions so students understand they can err when learning new things without judging their self-worth

Cultivating methods of thinking and doing that promote sound psychological and mental health
